description: The preferences a principal holds, and what each may be set to. spec-10 §20 forbids a code path supplying a value a registry omits, so a key's domain and its default are here and nowhere else.

theme.description: Which ramp the interface draws from. `system` is the third state A.10.1 requires be kept rather than resolved away, so what is stored is the person's intent and the resolved value is computed where it is rendered.

contrast.description: §14.5 names a contrast preference among the five that disclose a disability.

motion.description: §14.5 names a motion preference. §17.8 makes it govern more than duration: under it, transform animation, parallax, auto-advance and automatic preview are disabled whatever else is set.

density.description: A.1.6 gives density its values and no section says where a person's choice lives, so holding it here is this deployment's decision rather than a requirement. There is no media feature for how tightly a person wants things packed, so it has no `system` state.

text_size.description: §14.5 names a text size among the five. A proportion of the root size rather than a step, because A.1.3 has a rem honour the browser font size a person has already set and a step would discard it. 100 leaves that setting alone.

described_audio.description: §14.5 names a described-audio default among the five. Whether a described audio track is chosen where a holding carries one.

automatic_preview.description: §17.8: automatic preview of a holding on hover or focus "MUST default off, MUST be a per-principal preference, MUST be suppressed under reduced motion regardless of that preference". The suppression is not stored; it is read from the motion preference where a preview would start.

next_member_offer.description: §12.4 requires the end-of-item offer "be disableable per principal" and states no default. It is on, because the section makes the offer the behaviour and disabling it the choice.

language.description: The languages whose names this principal prefers, held as the language range spec-01 §7.4's resolution profile carries. A nomen's tag is matched against it by [RFC4647] §3.3.1 basic filtering rather than string equality, so `en` is matched by `en`, `en-GB` and `en-Latn-GB`. A request naming `language` narrows that request only and does not change what is held here.

caption_face.description: §17.4 requires caption presentation "be adjustable by the person, persisted per principal" and names no property of it, so these four are what this deployment draws. A caption is set in the same three families the rest of the interface has.

caption_size.description: A proportion of the caption's own base, which ranges further than body text because a caption is read at whatever distance the picture is watched from.

caption_ground.description: What sits behind the glyphs. A caption is drawn over moving picture rather than over a surface, so no contrast floor can be met by the ink alone: the ground is what makes one meetable, and removing it is a choice with `caption_edge` as its compensation.

caption_edge.description: How a glyph separates from the picture where the ground does not do it. Idle where the ground is solid.

browse_continue.description: §9.2: "A mode MAY be hidden per principal. Hiding a mode MUST NOT hide content." One key per mode rather than a list, because §9.2 fixes the seven and a key each keeps the set closed in the database. Continue is the requesting principal's own resume list.

browse_places.description: Places, as a list and as a map.

browse_time.description: A spine over time-spans, with a counted Undated bucket.
